To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) sexual activity is low, 2) consistent condom use is not high, and 3) condom use is lower among married couples.

(a) less than forty per cent of participants had had sexual intercourse in six months prior to survey; (b) marital status was the most important factor determining sexual activity; (c) consistent condom use during sexual intercourse was low; (d) consistent condom use was lowest in married and seroconcordance relationships; (e) the vast majority had disclosed their status; (f) qualitative data reinforced low rates; and (g) provided insights into sexual abstinences and condom use
sexual abstinence and seroconcordance are the most important factors in determining the sexual risk behaviour of HIV-positive people on ART in PNG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sexual practices of HIV-positive people on ART, but the implications are for the sexual health of the wider population in PNG.
how people living with HIV in PNG understand their sexual risk behaviour and the role of marriage and ART in this process.
the sexual practices of a group of people who have been largely ignored in the HIV prevention literature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majority of married HIV-positive people are sexually active, and the majority of those who are sexually active do not use condoms.
the sexual behaviour of HIV-positive people on ART is complex and is not adequately explained by the current HIV prevention messages.
sexual risk behaviour, marriage, and antiretrovial therapy are not necessarily mutually exclusive in PNG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sexual activity and sexual risk behaviour is low amongst people with HIV on antretroviral therapy, and condom use is low amongst married and seroconcordantly HIV-positive people.
HIV positive people on ART in PNG are more likely to be abstinent from sex than not.
sexual risk behaviour is a complex issue that requires a more nuanced approach to HIV prevention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV-positive people on ART are a diverse group with a range of sexual practices and needs.
the sexual behaviour of people on ART needs to be understood in the context of the social norms and practices that govern relationships in PNG.

the prevention of intimate partner HIV transmission in PNG requires an understanding of the complex interplay between sexual practices, marriage, ART, disclosure and the broader social and economic context.
